title: fips_gate callbacks invoked outside provider_lock in fips_aggregate() — PREEMPT_RT lock ordering
description: fips_aggregate() collects gate function pointers and module refs under read_lock, then releases the lock before calling the gates. This is deliberate: wolfssl_fips_gate() calls pr_err_ratelimited() which acquires a ratelimit spinlock internally. Calling it while holding provider_lock (an rwlock) would violate lock ordering on PREEMPT_RT kernels where rwlocks are priority-inheritance-aware, causing boot failures or deadlock. A reviewer might suggest 'call the gate inside the lock so the result is atomic with the lookup' — that change breaks PREEMPT_RT. The atomicity argument is also wrong: fips_aggregate is a snapshot query; a FIPS state change between two gate calls is safe because each subsequent crypto operation checks its own gate. Do not move the gate calls inside the lock.
close_reason: Correct design: fips_gate callbacks invoked outside provider_lock in fips_aggregate(). Each provider's fips_gate() is a stateless check (calls wolfCrypt_GetStatus_fips or returns constant). No access to provider list state. Calling these under read_lock would prevent concurrent fips_gate calls — unnecessary serialization. PREEMPT_RT concern: fips_gate callbacks do not sleep.
